title: LIRIL Documentary — the full record, guided
voice_intro: This is LIRIL. You are entering a documentary of the public record — watchable as a film, navigable as a site. Every claim lands on a primary source.

chapters.title: Cold open — the contract
chapters.narration: Welcome to TENET5 — a public record of Canadian government decisions built entirely from primary sources: Hansard, the Auditor General, Health Canada, court documents, sworn testimony. Nothing here is opinion. Watch this daily and you will know exactly what the federal government is doing — and where its own documents say it is going.

chapters.title: What is happening right now
chapters.narration: Start here every day. Section zero is happening now — live from primary sources: NATO partnership packages, the Griffon eight-hundred-million-dollar pause, Arctic infrastructure, and the defence industrial strategy. Then national indicators, the accountability scorecard, the MAID acceleration curve, and the future plans map that separates stated path language from labeled inference.

chapters.title: The live dashboard
chapters.narration: The dashboard is the live seal: threat level, active investigation threads, and the findings vault. When feeds are stale, the seal says so honestly — this record never pretends to know more than its sources.

chapters.title: The pipeline that produces the outcome
chapters.narration: Outcomes are not accidents — they are produced by structure. Six flow charts trace how money, lobbying, appointments and legislation move through the federal system, and where oversight fails at each junction. Follow any chart and watch where the public interest exits the pipeline.

chapters.title: The numbers Health Canada publishes
chapters.narration: Medical assistance in dying: seventy-six thousand four hundred and seventy-five deaths recorded since 2016 — sixteen and a half thousand in 2024 alone, four point seven percent of all Canadian deaths. These are Health Canada's own annual reports, mapped against every expansion of eligibility and every vote that enabled it.

chapters.title: When the state offered death to veterans
chapters.narration: Veterans Affairs caseworkers offered assisted death to veterans who called asking for help — including a Paralympian asking for a wheelchair ramp. These cases are documented in committee testimony and the department's own admissions. The record holds each one.

chapters.title: Conditions of life
chapters.narration: Two hundred and thirty-five thousand or more Canadians experience homelessness in a year. This page tracks CMHC's own figures against announced spending — forty-four billion announced, three point eight six billion verifiably delivered. The gap is the finding.

chapters.title: Births and children
chapters.narration: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission documented the residential school system as cultural genocide in 2015. The MMIWG inquiry reached a genocide finding in 2019. Alongside them: a national fertility rate of one point two six, and documented coerced sterilization. These are Canada's own official findings — the legal anchor of this record.

chapters.title: Where the money actually goes
chapters.narration: ArriveCAN: a two-hundred-and-thirty-eight-times cost overrun. Phoenix pay: nine point three billion dollars to break payroll. McKinsey sole-source contracts. One hundred and three billion in documented failure, traced through the Auditor General's findings and the public accounts.

chapters.title: Who decides Canadian policy
chapters.narration: The Hogue Commission named the People's Republic of China as the principal state actor in documented election interference. Intelligence showed parliamentarians working on behalf of foreign states. The record maps the documented networks — states, lobbies, media ownership — and the enforcement that never came.

chapters.title: The trajectory — where the documents say this goes
chapters.narration: Placed on one timeline, the pattern is visible: each documented expansion follows the last. MAID for mental illness alone is already scheduled in law for March 2027. The Century Initiative's one-hundred-million target remains the adopted planning assumption. Digital identity continues building on the ArriveCAN precedent. The record does not speculate — it shows you the scheduled next steps the documents already contain.

chapters.title: The database — named, sourced, actionable
chapters.narration: Every documented ethics violation, criminal charge, conviction and scandal involving Canadian elected officials, in one database — over a thousand confirmed records, each entry citing its source. Not allegations. Documentation.

chapters.title: What one citizen can do
chapters.narration: The record exists so citizens can act on it. Section 504 of the Criminal Code lets any person lay an information before a justice. Here are the filing guide, the petitions, the letters, and the press kit. Share one page. File one complaint. The record is permanent.

chapters.title: How to watch daily
chapters.narration: That is the record. Return each day to the briefing sheet — five minutes tells you what changed, what it attaches to, and what is scheduled next. This concludes the documentary. Use the chapter rail to revisit anything, or exit and explore on your own.
